reason: The cited evidence shows that laser cladding can deposit HEA coatings on steel (E2) and that RHEAs are considered for surface modification of TC4 (E1), but neither passage provides specific support for the key premises regarding bonding to TC4, preservation of TC4 bulk properties, or the quantitative hardness/wear improvements claimed. E2 demonstrates improved wear resistance via W-rich intermetallics and lattice distortion in a different substrate system, which loosely supports the mechanism but does not validate it for TC4.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit a RHEA coating on TC4 with a strong metallurgical bond
Refractory elements in RHEA induce lattice distortion and fine intermetallic precipitates that strengthen the coating
The RHEA coating will increase surface hardness by 1.5–2× and reduce friction/wear under high-stress, high-temperature conditions
The coating will remain homogeneous, well-bonded, and free of detrimental heat-affected zone issues under optimized parameters
The underlying TC4 bulk properties will be preserved
